Kupyn Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Kupyn's Jewish population reached an extraordinary 96.5 percent of the town by 1897, with Hasidism predominating locally. In March 1919, a pogrom was staged by Red Army troops — a notably rare attribution documented at several other towns in this collection, including Lyubar, Baranivka, and Rohachiv. In 1925, 35 Jewish families from Kupyn registered to relocate to the Kherson region, joining a broader wave of Jewish agricultural colonization documented elsewhere in this collection. In October 1941, 300 Jews were murdered by Ukrainian collaborationist police and buried in a mass grave directly at this cemetery; about 500 more were executed in late 1942.
